content.introduction: The sources indicate that the Schwab Center for Financial Research provides a six- to 12-month outlook for stock sectors, known as Schwab Sector Views. This outlook combines a factor-based approach with a market and economic assessment to determine ratings on the 11 S&P 500 equity sectors. The views reflect preferences for investment assets relative to their peers and may change as markets evolve. The outlook does not guarantee future returns and is not a forecast that an asset will rise or fall. The most recent outlook available is from October 30, 2026, which highlights the favorability of the lending sector due to strong balance sheets and lower valuations compared to the broader market.

_Schwab Sector Views is our six- to 12-month outlook for stock sectors, which represent broad sectors of the economy. The Schwab Center for Financial Research (SCFR) combines a factor-based approach with a market and economic assessment to determine the ratings. For the basics on sectors, please see__Stock Sectors: What Are They? How Are They Used?_ [...] Investors who want to make tactical shifts in their portfolios can use Schwab Sector Views ratings as a resource. These ratings can be helpful in evaluating and monitoring the domestic equity portion of a portfolio. These favorability views are our preferences for investment assets relative to their peers shown in each section. The views reflect a six- to 12-month outlook and may change as markets evolve. Views do not guarantee future returns and are not a forecast that an asset will rise or [...] balance sheets tend to support lenders, and the sector continues to trade at lower valuations than the broader market. Current earnings revisions, net interest income, and capital markets trends may provide a favorable backdrop for the group.
